nodes.Name: Valid
nodes.DocComment: Valid reports whether data is a valid JSON encoding.

nodes.Name: checkValid
nodes.DocComment:
checkValid verifies that data is valid JSON-encoded data.
scan is passed in for use by checkValid to avoid an allocation.
checkValid returns nil or a SyntaxError.

nodes.Name: SyntaxError
nodes.DocComment:
A SyntaxError is a description of a JSON syntax error.
[Unmarshal] will return a SyntaxError if the JSON can't be parsed.

Fields.Name: Offset
Fields.DocComment: error occurred after reading Offset bytes

nodes.Name: scanner
nodes.DocComment:
A scanner is a JSON scanning state machine.
Callers call scan.reset and then pass bytes in one at a time
by calling scan.step(&scan, c) for each byte.
The return value, referred to as an opcode, tells the
caller about significant parsing events like beginning
and ending literals, objects, and arrays, so that the
caller can follow along if it wishes.
The return value scanEnd indicates that a single top-level
JSON value has been completed, *before* the byte that
just got passed in.  (The indication must be delayed in order
to recognize the end of numbers: is 123 a whole value or
the beginning of 12345e+6?).

nodes.Name: scanContinue
nodes.DocComment:
These values are returned by the state transition functions
assigned to scanner.state and the method scanner.eof.
They give details about the current state of the scan that
callers might be interested to know about.
It is okay to ignore the return value of any particular
call to scanner.state: if one call returns scanError,
every subsequent call will return scanError too.

nodes.Name: parseObjectKey
nodes.DocComment:
These values are stored in the parseState stack.
They give the current state of a composite value
being scanned. If the parser is inside a nested value
the parseState describes the nested state, outermost at entry 0.

nodes.DocComment:

nodes.Name: maxNestingDepth
nodes.DocComment:
This limits the max nesting depth to prevent stack overflow.
This is permitted by https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-9

nodes.Name: reset
nodes.DocComment:
reset prepares the scanner for use.
It must be called before calling s.step.

nodes.Name: eof
nodes.DocComment:
eof tells the scanner that the end of input has been reached.
It returns a scan status just as s.step does.

nodes.Name: pushParseState
nodes.DocComment:
pushParseState pushes a new parse state newParseState onto the parse stack.
an error state is returned if maxNestingDepth was exceeded, otherwise successState is returned.

nodes.Name: popParseState
nodes.DocComment:
popParseState pops a parse state (already obtained) off the stack
and updates s.step accordingly.

nodes.Name: stateBeginValueOrEmpty
nodes.DocComment: stateBeginValueOrEmpty is the state after reading `[`.

nodes.Name: stateBeginValue
nodes.DocComment: stateBeginValue is the state at the beginning of the input.

nodes.Name: stateBeginStringOrEmpty
nodes.DocComment: stateBeginStringOrEmpty is the state after reading `{`.

nodes.Name: stateBeginString
nodes.DocComment: stateBeginString is the state after reading `{"key": value,`.

nodes.Name: stateEndValue
nodes.DocComment:
stateEndValue is the state after completing a value,
such as after reading `{}` or `true` or `["x"`.

nodes.Name: stateEndTop
nodes.DocComment:
stateEndTop is the state after finishing the top-level value,
such as after reading `{}` or `[1,2,3]`.
Only space characters should be seen now.

nodes.Name: stateInString
nodes.DocComment: stateInString is the state after reading `"`.

nodes.Name: stateInStringEsc
nodes.DocComment: stateInStringEsc is the state after reading `"\` during a quoted string.

nodes.Name: stateInStringEscU
nodes.DocComment: stateInStringEscU is the state after reading `"\u` during a quoted string.

nodes.Name: stateInStringEscU1
nodes.DocComment: stateInStringEscU1 is the state after reading `"\u1` during a quoted string.

nodes.Name: stateInStringEscU12
nodes.DocComment: stateInStringEscU12 is the state after reading `"\u12` during a quoted string.

nodes.Name: stateInStringEscU123
nodes.DocComment: stateInStringEscU123 is the state after reading `"\u123` during a quoted string.

nodes.Name: stateNeg
nodes.DocComment: stateNeg is the state after reading `-` during a number.

nodes.Name: state1
nodes.DocComment:
state1 is the state after reading a non-zero integer during a number,
such as after reading `1` or `100` but not `0`.

nodes.Name: state0
nodes.DocComment: state0 is the state after reading `0` during a number.

nodes.Name: stateDot
nodes.DocComment:
stateDot is the state after reading the integer and decimal point in a number,
such as after reading `1.`.

nodes.Name: stateDot0
nodes.DocComment:
stateDot0 is the state after reading the integer, decimal point, and subsequent
digits of a number, such as after reading `3.14`.

nodes.Name: stateE
nodes.DocComment:
stateE is the state after reading the mantissa and e in a number,
such as after reading `314e` or `0.314e`.

nodes.Name: stateESign
nodes.DocComment:
stateESign is the state after reading the mantissa, e, and sign in a number,
such as after reading `314e-` or `0.314e+`.

nodes.Name: stateE0
nodes.DocComment:
stateE0 is the state after reading the mantissa, e, optional sign,
and at least one digit of the exponent in a number,
such as after reading `314e-2` or `0.314e+1` or `3.14e0`.

nodes.Name: stateT
nodes.DocComment: stateT is the state after reading `t`.

nodes.Name: stateTr
nodes.DocComment: stateTr is the state after reading `tr`.

nodes.Name: stateTru
nodes.DocComment: stateTru is the state after reading `tru`.

nodes.Name: stateF
nodes.DocComment: stateF is the state after reading `f`.

nodes.Name: stateFa
nodes.DocComment: stateFa is the state after reading `fa`.

nodes.Name: stateFal
nodes.DocComment: stateFal is the state after reading `fal`.

nodes.Name: stateFals
nodes.DocComment: stateFals is the state after reading `fals`.

nodes.Name: stateN
nodes.DocComment: stateN is the state after reading `n`.

nodes.Name: stateNu
nodes.DocComment: stateNu is the state after reading `nu`.

nodes.Name: stateNul
nodes.DocComment: stateNul is the state after reading `nul`.

nodes.Name: stateError
nodes.DocComment:
stateError is the state after reaching a syntax error,
such as after reading `[1}` or `5.1.2`.

nodes.Name: error
nodes.DocComment: error records an error and switches to the error state.

nodes.Name: quoteChar
nodes.DocComment: quoteChar formats c as a quoted character literal.
